A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SemHiTok and its unified multimodal model. Their text, equations, figures and tables are readable, including v5's technical appendices. v4 ends with references and has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v4 reports original image reconstruction, multimodal understanding, text-to-image generation and ablation results in Section 4.

after.justification: v5 retains original experiments and adds generation benchmarks, controlled ablations and quantitative pixel-consistency results in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The hierarchical codebook, staged semantic/pixel training, quantization objectives, codebook flattening and Dual-MLP adapter are retained. v5's Algorithm 1 documents deployment and embedding handling more explicitly; the PDFs do not establish that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: v5 adds GenEval and DPG evaluation to the existing text-to-image coverage (Appendix 7.6, Table 7). Reconstruction, multimodal understanding and the training-data families remain covered. This is a limited benchmark expansion within the existing generation task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership changes substantially. UniTok disappears from both understanding comparison tables, while v5 adds comparisons involving TokenFlow, Janus-Pro, UniToken and SynerGen-VL, among others. UniToken is a distinct cited method, not a renaming of UniTok. New reconstruction comparisons include QLIP-B, FSQ, LFQ, SimVQ and Open-MAGVIT2. SDE/MUSE-VL is matched as the same work.

E3.justification: v5 adds 384-resolution tokenizer understanding evaluation, controls comparing structure and training strategy, a DCT-based VRR protocol, and comparisons controlling total codebook size (Tables 2, 6 and 12–13; Appendix 7.9). It also changes the reported MLLM pretraining MidJourney sample count from 12M to 15M. This is a reported setting revision, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the existing component, concatenation and VQ ablations, v5 tests joint versus staged training and architectural separation (Table 6), semantic codebook size and capacity allocation (Tables 11–13), and quantitative pixel similarity within codes (Table 8). Figure 8 also supplies additional reconstruction outputs for module comparisons. These substantially strengthen investigation of the design rationale.

E5.justification: v4 reports no repeated-run uncertainty estimates. v5's new VRR analysis reports five independent sampling runs using 10K ImageNet validation images and displays ± values in Table 8. The statistic represented by ± is unspecified, and uncertainty reporting is not extended to the main benchmark results.

E6.justification: The original headline scores remain, including rFID 1.16/0.66 and MJHQ30K gFID 5.40/5.70. However, v5 adds substantial result sets: 384-resolution tokenizer understanding scores, GenEval 0.71 and DPG 83.59, VRR measurements, training-strategy controls and codebook-size comparisons. Comparator additions and removals also change reported result entries. These are expanded results, not established performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix 7.9 introduces code-conditioned DCT variance quantities and defines VRR = 1 − Vmean/Vglobal for the new analysis. The original quantization, EMA, reconstruction-loss and flattening mathematics remain unchanged. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a hierarchical tokenizer that reconciles semantic and pixel information, compatibility with next-token models, and strong understanding and generation performance. v5 softens some abstract wording and emphasizes additional validation, but retains the underlying contribution and performance claims, including the MJHQ30K claim in Section 3.3.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations concerning structural efficiency versus combinatorial codebook capacity, the effects of joint training and naive feature combination, and tighter pixel clustering under semantic conditioning. Section 6 newly acknowledges generation cost from long image-token sequences and unexplored reasoning post-training, while identifying image editing and multiround conversations as future work. These materially expand mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v5 adds special-token and embedding-processing instructions, deployment pseudocode, GPU counts, training durations and guidance scale 2.5; it also identifies the Instruct base-model variant and promises code/weight release. Conversely, v4's training table with stage-specific learning rates and batch sizes is removed, along with exact SigLIP variants and explicit pixel-codebook normalization details. These are substantial documentation changes with mixed reproducibility effects.

R1.justification: v5 substantially expands the cited comparison landscape with newer unified models and quantizers, including Janus-Pro, UniToken, QLIP, Tar, SimVQ and Open-MAGVIT2. It adds discussion positioning SGHC against FQGAN and combinatorial quantization capacity. Some earlier works, including Efficient-VQGAN and Unified-IO 2, disappear; citation-style and SDE/MUSE-VL publication updates are not counted as new works.

P1.justification: Related work moves from before the method to after the experiments, ablation becomes a standalone section, and substantial setup, visualization and existing ablation material moves into a technical appendix. The introduction, results discussion and conclusion are revised, with new structural/training terminology and deployment explanations. This is substantial narrative reorganization beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v5 redraws Figure 1, removes v4's dual-tokenizer diagram and characteristics/training tables, clarifies the architecture diagram, replaces token counts with code shapes, and adds training-image columns. It introduces new analysis tables and reconstruction panels and revises the understanding examples. The generation gallery is retained and relocated, rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: The new controlled ablations and quantitative pixel-consistency analysis provide stronger support for SGHC's central rationale, while deployment documentation and explicit limitations improve transparency. These gains are tempered by removal of v4's learning-rate/batch-size table and an inconsistent capacity label in v5 Table 13: 16,384 × 8 is printed as 262,144. The added evidence supports a net improvement, but reproducibility losses and reporting errors limit its extent.
